claims.text: Every stall weighs on the town's checked scale.
Hill farmers may sell by their own basket measure.
Every price is posted before anyone bargains.
The market opens at dawn, even if the weights inspector is late.
Every sale over ten coins is written in the market book.

clashes.line: Both rules stand, and they disagree about every sack the hill farmers bring. The meeting will have to come back to this.
Both rules stand. On mornings when the inspector is late, the stalls open with scales nobody has checked.

others.why: Tellen puts everything on rules a stranger could check. 'A market is only fair if a buyer who knows nobody can still trust it.'
Dagny puts nothing on the market book. 'Half the hill families cannot read it, and the other half do not want the town counting their sales.'

values.text: That a stranger can trust what they are sold.
values.reply: Tellen nods. 'Then you will want proof that everyone can check. Be ready for the people who feel checked.'

values.text: That people keep their own ways of measuring.
values.reply: Dagny smiles. 'Then you will need to explain the basket to every stranger who buys from it. That is work too.'

values.text: That traders can make a living today.
values.reply: Tellen and Dagny both nod. 'Today,' says Dagny. 'And next year, when a buyer comes back angry?' asks Tellen. A living depends on both.
